about: Golden vectors for the pix3-rooms wire protocol, shared by every implementation.
Every expected value here was derived BY HAND from the offset, encoding and rounding tables in
docs/protocol.md — never captured from a run of a codec. A vector produced by the code under test
would only prove that the code agrees with itself; these fail the moment an offset, a width, an
endianness or a rounding mode drifts away from the published contract.
Verified from two sides: tests/Pix3.Rooms.Tests/Protocol/GoldenVectorFileTests.cs checks the C#
codec against this file, and packages/pix3-runtime/src/net/protocol/protocol.spec.ts (in the pix3
repo, which holds a stamped copy) checks the hand-written TypeScript codec against the same bytes.
Hex strings ignore whitespace. Float inputs are written as decimals that are exactly representable
in float32, so widening them to double is lossless and both languages read the same number; the
three rotation cases that are not exactly representable carry an explicit float32 bit pattern
instead, because a decimal literal there would round differently in the two languages.

position.name: far corner
position.why: 4096 x 65535 / 4096 = 65535 exactly, the top of the range

rotation.name: negative quarter turn wraps first
rotation.why: wraps to 3pi/2 -> 0.75 x 256; the wrap happens before the scale

rotation.name: just under a full turn folds to zero
a hair below zero folds to zero
rotation.why: wraps to just under 2pi and folds the same way

nonFinite.why: Non-finite input is refused and counted, never quantized: one NaN poisons the spatial hash.

sample.why: One entity reused throughout, chosen so no two fields share a value and every multi-byte field has distinguishable high and low bytes, so a swapped endianness cannot pass.
sample.flagsNote: 0xA9 = 1010_1001: policy bits 0-1 = 01 (Shared), fabric reserved bit 2 clear, app bits 3-7 = 10101

vectors.name: FullRecord
vectors.why: 0 u32 NetId, 4 u16 Kind, 6 u32 OwnerId, 10 u16 QX, 12 u16 QY, 14 u8 QRot, 15 i16 QVx, 17 i16 QVy, 19 u8 Flags

vectors.name: UpdateRecord/typical moving entity
vectors.why: u16 Slot + mask + QX + QY + QRot = the 8 bytes the bandwidth budget is built on

vectors.name: UpdateRecord/every field
vectors.why: 0x3F | 0x80: every payload bit plus Teleport, which contributes no bytes. The 13-byte maximum.

vectors.name: UpdateRecord/signal bits only
vectors.why: ColdDirty | Teleport carry no payload: a bare 3-byte header

vectors.name: UpdateRecord/rot and flags only
vectors.why: Fields appear in bit order; a decoder that mis-ordered them would land QRot on Flags

vectors.name: OwnerUpdateRecord/x and y
vectors.why: Keyed by u32 NetId rather than slot, so the server can reject a mutation aimed at a reused slot

vectors.name: RemovedSlot
vectors.why: A removal record is a bare little-endian slot

vectors.name: SnapshotPacket/one record, final
vectors.why: 0 u8 TypeId 68, 1 u16 Seq, 3 u32 ServerTick, 7 u8 FrameFlags, 8 u16 Count, then FullRecord x Count

vectors.name: SnapshotPacket/empty but final
vectors.why: A snapshot is always sent, even when empty: a joiner who can see nothing must still be told the snapshot is complete

vectors.name: DeltaPacket/empty
vectors.why: All three counts are always present, even when zero: 7 + 3 x 2 = 13 bytes of fixed overhead

vectors.name: DeltaPacket/one of each section
vectors.why: Sections are interleaved (count, then its records, then the next count), removals first so a slot's removal always precedes any reuse of it

vectors.name: EntityUpdatePacket
vectors.why: 0 u8 TypeId 67, 1 u32 ClientTick, 5 u8 Count, 6 OwnerUpdateRecord x Count

vectors.name: SignalBatchPacket/two entries
vectors.why: 8-byte header then (u32 Sender, u8 NameLength, name, u8 PayloadLength, payload) per entry; one entry is 6 + NameLength + PayloadLength bytes

why: MemoryPack version-tolerant objects: [u8 memberCount][varint ByteLength x memberCount][values].
See docs/protocol.md -> Control-plane encoding. These vectors exercise every encoding rule the
format has: the empty object, each primitive width, ASCII and non-ASCII strings, the empty and
null string, empty and null arrays, nested string[]/byte[][], and a member length that crosses

vectors.note: An empty message is a lone memberCount of zero
The load-bearing non-ASCII case: 12 UTF-8 bytes but a UTF-16 length of 6. A client that writes the byte count in both slots produces text C# mis-sizes.
A surrogate pair: 4 UTF-8 bytes, UTF-16 length 2

vectors.name: empty string
vectors.note: An empty string is the non-negative UTF-16 length zero, not a UTF-8 header
An empty byte[] is a collection header of zero, distinct from the null FFFFFFFF
Nine members. Spawn carries quantized fields, not floats, so it cannot introduce a value the delta plane could not express.
string[] and byte[][]: a collection header of element count, then that many fully-encoded elements

vectors.name: empty but final
vectors.note: A roster is always sent, even when it would be empty: a client must be told the roster is complete. Three members, so three declared lengths: two empty collection headers and the flags byte.

vectors.name: two members, final
vectors.note: uint[] is a collection header of element count then 4 bytes each: 4 + 8 = 12. string[] is 4 + (4 + 4 + 3) + (4 + 4 + 2) = 25.

vectors.name: a chunk that is not the last
vectors.note: FrameFlags 0: a self-contained chunk of a roster that continues. Only the last chunk carries Final.

vectors.name: non-ASCII display name
vectors.note: The UTF-16-length-vs-byte-count trap, inside an array: 12 UTF-8 bytes but a UTF-16 length of 6, so the member is 4 + (4 + 4 + 12) = 24 — and a sender that sized its chunks by character count would overflow the frame cap.

vectors.name: fresh join, null resume key
vectors.note: A fresh join and a resume attempt differ only by this member: null array is FFFFFFFF, still a declared length of 4

vectors.name: token crossing the single-byte varint boundary
vectors.note: The Token member is 4 + 4 + 120 = 128 bytes, one past the raw-byte range, so its length is the marker 0x84 followed by a u16. A real JWT lands here, which is why this case is pinned. ~120 = -121 = 87FFFFFF.

vectors.name: the answer to a resumed Hello
vectors.note: The largest control message, at sixteen members, and the only one carrying a float or a bool — so it is what pins those two primitive encodings. Floats are IEEE-754 little-endian: AoiRadius 512 is 00000044, and the world bounds -2048 / 4096 are 000000C5 / 00008045.
